neighbours.label: a market-activity noun naming flows of buying, supplying or hiring (supply, buying, hiring, spending, purchasing) in an economic context
fire: Analysts expect the oil supply to tighten again next winter.
Rising wages have boosted the buying power of young workers.
The hiring process at the bank now includes two video interviews.
Consumer spending slowed sharply in the third quarter.
The company's purchasing department signed a new contract with vendors.
Port closures left global supply chains in disarray.
Holiday shopping has shifted toward online stores this year.
Weak demand led many retailers to freeze hiring until spring.
quiet: Analysts expect the interest rate to rise again next winter.
Rising wages have increased the tax burden of young workers.
The annual report at the bank now includes two new appendices.
The discount rate stayed unchanged in the third quarter.
The company's legal department reviewed a new contract with landlords.
The central bank's decision left global interest rates unchanged.
Holiday weather has shifted toward warmer winters this year.
Weak demand led many central banks to cut interest rates until spring.

notes: Card: ' supply' x15, ' buying' x5, ' hiring', ' spending', ' purchasing', ' credit'; the - pole is interest/discount rates. Near misses keep the economic setting but name rates, taxes or reports instead.
